review.tagline: Python tool that trains neural models to swap faces in images and video
review.summary: FaceSwap is a Python program with three stages run through `faceswap.py`: extract faces from photos or video frames, train a model on two sets of faces, and convert source media with the trained model. It ships a Tkinter-style GUI (`faceswap.py gui`) alongside the CLI, and includes models such as Villain and Phaze-A. It runs on Windows, Linux and macOS, with CUDA GPUs recommended and some AMD support via ROCm on Linux.
review.audience: Hobbyists and VFX users training face-swap models on their own GPU
strengths: Covers the full workflow: extract, train and convert, via CLI or GUI
Multiple model architectures named in the README, including Villain, Phaze-A, DFL-H128 and DFaker
Runs on Windows, Linux and macOS; AMD GPUs supported via ROCm on Linux
Existing models can be reused to shorten training on new faces
weaknesses: Training requires a modern CUDA GPU for acceptable speed; exact VRAM needs are unknown
No Docker or compose setup in the repo
Setup problems are directed to the forum and Discord, not GitHub issues
Manual workflow: gathering and curating face data is left to the user
needs: Models: Villain, Phaze-A, DFL-H128, DFaker, Unbalanced
